channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Former Deputy Interior Minister Reorganizes Profitable Real Estate Fund
item.description: Former Kazakh Deputy Interior Minister Vasily Simachev and other shareholders are reorganizing the 'Alba' real estate investment fund from a joint-stock company to a limited liability partnership. The fund reported a profit of 215 million tenge in 2025, with rental income increasing to 182.4 million tenge.

item.title: Estonia secures EU sanctions exemption for Russian rare metals supplier
item.description: Estonia has successfully lobbied for the exclusion of a Russian rare metals supplier and an associated individual from the EU's 22nd sanctions package. This exemption is due to Europe's industrial dependence on the strategic raw materials supplied by the company to NPM Silmet.

item.title: Documentary on Afghan Activist Zarqa Yaftali Wins Silver Dolphin at Cannes Awards
item.description: A documentary about Afghan education and women's rights activist Zarqa Yaftali has won the Silver Dolphin award at the 2026 Cannes Media and Television Awards. The film, "Educating Hope in Afghanistan: The Story of Zarqa," highlights her work supporting girls' education and women's rights amid Taliban restrictions.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Public Debt Surpasses $10 Billion Amid Rising Repayment Costs
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's public debt reached $10.16 billion by the end of July 2026. The government anticipates spending approximately $1.83 billion on external debt servicing between 2027 and 2029. External debt stood at $5.19 billion, with domestic debt at $4.96 billion. The total debt represents about 38% of the projected 2026 GDP.

item.title: Aquatherm Tashkent 2026: Turkish Company Expands Presence in Uzbekistan Market
item.description: The Turkish company Ayvaz is expanding its operations in Uzbekistan, participating in the Aquatherm Tashkent 2026 exhibition. The company, founded in 1948, offers products like compensators and fire safety equipment. Ayvaz recently opened a new representative office, 'Yuroturk,' in Tashkent to foster business contacts and partnerships.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Revise 10th-11th Grade Curriculum Following Textbook Scandal
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to revise its 10th and 11th-grade school programs, including the literature list, after a scandal erupted over a Russian language and literature textbook. The textbook contained an explicit scene involving Sultan Baibars and a young girl, drawing public outrage. The curriculum review follows an expert evaluation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Adopts Declaration for Human Oversight of Artificial Intelligence in the Workplace
item.description: Kazakhstan's government, employers, and trade unions signed a declaration in Astana calling for human oversight of AI decisions affecting workers' rights. The declaration, adopted at the 'Digital Labor and Artificial Intelligence' forum, emphasizes employer accountability and the right for workers to challenge AI-driven decisions. Kazakhstan's existing AI legislation and Digital Code also provide for transparency and human review of automated decisions.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Revise Clinic Evaluation System, Prioritizing Patient Feedback
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Health announced a revised clinic evaluation system that will incorporate patient feedback. The new system will assess factors like wait times for specialist appointments, timely diagnostic tests, and post-discharge follow-up. A 100-point unified system will be implemented, with data automatically calculated quarterly based on information from healthcare information systems.

item.title: New Benefit Requirements in Kazakhstan: Payments to Cease for Some from 2027
item.description: From 2027, Kazakhstan will change the procedure for assigning several state benefits, introducing a needs-based principle. Citizens in higher social welfare categories A and B will not receive these payments. The changes affect benefits for childbirth, childcare, large families, disability, and loss of a breadwinner, among others.

item.title: Almaty City Hall Responds to Complaints About Unsafe Wheelchair Ramps
item.description: Almaty authorities will repair unsafe wheelchair ramps on the updated Republic Square following resident complaints. A citizen highlighted damaged ramps and questioned their usability for people with disabilities and parents with strollers, noting a step at the top of some ramps. The city's public spaces department acknowledged the issue and will ensure safe access.

item.title: Almaty Residents Complain About Unusable Ramp on Newly Renovated Republic Square
item.description: Almaty residents have reported that mothers with strollers must carry them up stairs due to an inconvenient ramp on Republic Square. The city's public spaces department acknowledged the ramp near the fountains requires repair and will be restored to ensure safe access for all pedestrians, including those with limited mobility.

item.title: Three Killed in Saudi Arabia Airport Attacks; Houthi Rebels Claim Responsibility
item.description: Three people were killed and 36 injured in two separate attacks on Saudi Arabian airports, Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport. The Saudi Civil Aviation Authority confirmed the incidents. Houthi rebels claimed responsibility for the attacks, stating they used drones and ballistic missiles.

item.title: Hundreds of Turkmen Citizens Fighting in Ukraine for Russian Army; Ukrainian Officials in Talks with Turkmen Side
item.description: Hundreds of Turkmen citizens are fighting in the Russian army in Ukraine, with reports indicating an increase in recruitment due to severe unemployment and labor migration in Turkmenistan. Ukrainian officials are reportedly in talks with the Turkmen side regarding these fighters, with at least 61 confirmed deaths among them.

item.title: Kazakhstan Uncovers Thousands of Cases Selling Expired and Free Medications
item.description: Kazakhstan has identified the sale of 27,000 packages of medications intended for free distribution. The Ministry of Trade and Integration reported that the digital marking system for medicines revealed these violations. Additionally, 7,500 cases of expired drug sales and over 470,000 instances of repackaged medicines with the same code were found. The system tracks drug movement and sales across the country.

item.title: East Kazakhstan Region Expands Radiation Therapy with Second Linear Accelerator
item.description: The oncology center in the East Kazakhstan region has enhanced its radiation therapy capabilities with the installation of a second linear accelerator, an Elekta Versa HD unit. This upgrade, supported by the "Kazakhstan Khalkyna" fund, aims to increase specialized care and ensure treatment continuity for the region's approximately 15,000 cancer patients. The new equipment will help manage over 2,500 new cases diagnosed annually.

item.title: South Korea Recalls Ambassador to Ukraine Amid Tensions After North Korea's Disclosure
item.description: South Korea has recalled its ambassador to Ukraine following tensions that arose after North Korea disclosed the dispatch of its soldiers to Seoul. Despite Ukraine officially apologizing, Seoul was not satisfied and took a strong measure. The situation escalated after North Korea revealed its soldiers were sent to Seoul, prompting South Korea to demand an apology from Kyiv.

item.title: Almaty SuperSki Project to Launch in 2028, Focusing on Sustainable Tourism
item.description: The Almaty SuperSki project, set to launch in 2028, will utilize 20 hectares for tourism infrastructure, prioritizing natural landscape preservation. The resort aims to accommodate over 10,000 visitors daily and boost year-round tourism, including summer activities like hiking and cycling.

item.title: Akmola Region Prosecutors Secure 11 Million Tenge in Compensation for 68 Pensioners
item.description: Prosecutors in the Tselinograd district of the Akmola region have restored the labor and constitutional rights of 68 pensioners. Following an investigation into labor law violations, the pensioners received a total of 11 million tenge in compensation for improper termination of employment.

item.title: Kazakhstan Appoints Former Finance Official as Deputy Defense Minister Amid Investigation
item.description: President Tokayev appointed Tatyana Savelyeva as deputy defense minister on October 7, following an investigation into the ministry after 14 service members died. Savelyeva, formerly vice minister of finance, replaces Asker Beisenov. She resigned from parliament to take the role. Her appointment is linked to ongoing corruption probes within the ministry.

item.title: Uzbekistan Dok-1 Max Victims Still Await Most Compensation Over Two Years Later
item.description: Families affected by Uzbekistan's Dok-1 Max poisoning scandal are still owed most of the 78 billion soums awarded in compensation. This follows a court verdict over two years ago. The scandal, linked to 68 child deaths, involved contaminated cold medicines manufactured by India's Marion Biotech. A court sentenced 23 defendants in February 2024.

item.title: Turkmen Soldiers' Families Report Poor Conditions, Demand Daily Payments for Food
item.description: Families of conscripted soldiers in Turkmenistan report dire conditions in military units, citing poor sanitation, inadequate food, and water shortages. Parents claim they must send 50-150 manats daily to ensure their sons receive sufficient food. Soldiers reportedly suffer from skin diseases due to unsanitary living conditions.

item.title: Tajikistan to Host Central Asia-USA Business Forum in April 2027
item.description: Tajikistan is preparing to host the third Central Asia-USA Business Forum (B5+1) in Dushanbe in April 2027. A preliminary event was held in Washington on October 7th, attended by officials and business representatives. The forum aims to strengthen economic and investment cooperation, focusing on areas like AI, IT, fintech, e-commerce, and strategic minerals.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Public Trust in AI for Healthcare: A Mixed Picture
item.description: A STADA Health Report 2026 study reveals 55% of Uzbekistan's population uses AI for health-related matters, with 69% among those under 35. While AI is seen as a supplementary tool, not a doctor replacement, 47% are hesitant to trust AI diagnoses as much as medical professionals'. A presentation in Tashkent discussed these findings.

item.title: Almaty to Spend Over 500 Million Tenge on Public Transport Fare Inspectors
item.description: Almaty's transport authority will allocate over 556 million tenge to hire and deploy fare inspectors on buses and trolleybuses. The plan requires at least 80 inspectors daily, with a total workforce of 200. Inspectors will monitor fare payment on public transport routes, ensuring compliance and data recording through specialized terminals and GPS tracking.

item.title: US Assesses Kazakhstan's Investment Climate, Highlighting Investor Concerns
item.description: The US State Department views Kazakhstan as a key market for foreign investment in Central Asia. However, a recent report identifies rule of law, corruption, unpredictable regulation, and a new tax code as significant risk factors for investors. Despite substantial foreign investment, particularly in oil and gas, these issues raise concerns.

item.title: Court Sentence Issued for Son of Former Kyrgyz President
item.description: A court in Kyrgyzstan has issued a sentence for the son of a former president. The details of the charges and the specific sentence were not provided in the source material, but the case involves a former head of state's family.

item.title: Taliban Interference in Zabul Aid Distribution Diverts Resources from Needy
item.description: Residents of Zabul province report that the Taliban are interfering with humanitarian aid distribution, channeling it to relatives and affiliates. Aid workers coordinate with the group out of fear, leading to aid reaching ineligible individuals. Sources claim only half the aid reaches the intended recipients.

item.title: Astana court sentences fraudster for deceiving young footballers' parents
item.description: A fraudster in Astana has been sentenced to three years and two months in prison for deceiving parents of young footballers. The accused promised to organize trips to an international tournament in Spain, collecting over 24 million tenge from nine victims for participation, flights, and visas, but never fulfilled the obligations. The stolen funds have been recovered.

item.title: Dushanbe to Host SCO Transport and Logistics International Exhibition
item.description: An international exhibition titled 'SCO Transport and Logistics' will be held in Dushanbe from October 19-20, coinciding with the 25th anniversary of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO). The event aims to showcase member states' potential in transport and logistics, foster business partnerships, and discuss seamless logistical routes within the SCO space.

item.title: Afghan Asylum Seekers in India Face Prolonged Delays, Limited Support
item.description: Afghan women seeking asylum in India report years-long delays in case processing, leaving their futures uncertain. Lack of residency and work permits hinders employment and living expenses. Reduced aid since 2024 and difficulties accessing healthcare exacerbate their situation, impacting children's education.

item.title: WHO Does Not Confirm New Illness Cases in Irkutsk Region
item.description: The World Health Organization (WHO) has not confirmed new illness cases among individuals who contacted an employee of the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute diagnosed with pneumonia. Rospotrebnadzor stated that the WHO has no confirmed information on new cases and has received full details on measures taken, confirming no public health risks.

item.title: UN Mission Reports Over 50 Women Detained by Taliban for Dress Code Violations
item.description: The UN mission in Afghanistan reported that Taliban authorities detained at least 52 women and one girl in Kabul and Herat over three months for alleged dress code violations. Reasons included visible hair, colorful scarves, or appearing in public without a male guardian. UNAMA expressed grave concern, stating these acts violate women's rights and could lead to social stigma.

item.title: Central Asian and Azerbaijani Leaders Hold Consultative Meeting in Turkmenistan
item.description: Heads of state from Central Asia and Azerbaijan convened for a consultative meeting in Turkmenistan's Avaza National Tourist Zone. Presidents from Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan participated. The meeting aimed to foster dialogue and address regional cooperation within Central Asia.

item.title: Human Rights Groups Urge Tashkent to Free Karakalpak Activist Tajimuratov and Investigate Torture Claims
item.description: International human rights organizations are calling for the immediate release of Karakalpak activist Dauletmurat Tajimuratov from prison and for an investigation into his torture allegations. The groups demand his safety, medical care, and compensation, urging the international community to support these demands.

item.title: Tajikistan President Proposes New Refinery; Kyrgyzstan Ready to Buy Oil Products
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon reiterated his proposal for a large oil refinery to serve Central Asia. Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov stated Bishkek is willing to purchase petroleum products from regional countries at market prices and explore joint production.

item.title: Uzbekistan Pursues Regional Economic Integration and Diversified Export Routes
item.description: Uzbekistan is enhancing regional economic integration and diversifying export routes, aiming to overcome geographical limitations. President Mirziyeyev's visit to Turkmenistan focuses on expanding export opportunities and reducing reliance on limited transit paths. Discussions include political coordination, trade, energy, transport, and security.

item.title: First Housing Subsidy Selection for Medical Workers to Be Held October 9
item.description: The first selection for housing subsidies for medical and pharmaceutical staff will take place on October 9. 125 winners will be chosen from 1,657 eligible candidates via an automatic random selection process, as reported by the Ministry of Health. This initiative aims to support healthcare professionals in purchasing homes.

item.title: Extensive Russian Attacks on Ukraine Result in at Least 32 Casualties
item.description: Widespread Russian attacks targeting Ukraine have led to a significant loss of life, with at least 32 individuals confirmed dead. The scale of the assaults indicates a severe escalation of the conflict, causing substantial human casualties and damage across Ukrainian territories.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan Sign Agreement to Establish High-Level Strategic Partnership Council
item.description: Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan have signed an agreement to establish a High-Level Strategic Partnership Council. This initiative aims to deepen bilateral relations, enhance political dialogue, and expand practical cooperation in priority areas. The agreement was signed following a meeting between Presidents Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Serdar Berdimuhamedov.

item.title: Son of Kyrgyzstan's Former President Sentenced to Four Years in Prison
item.description: Kadyr Atambayev, son of former Kyrgyz President Almazbek Atambayev, has been sentenced to four years in a general regime colony for plotting a violent power seizure. The court found him and other Social Democrats party members guilty. Another party member received a suspended sentence, while a former MP was acquitted.
